note: The two sets are nearly identical; A adds two extra claims that B omits: a second 'axial stiffness 0 N at r/R = 1.0' (a straight duplicate of a claim B already has) and a 'mass density 0 kg/m at r/R = 1.0' that conflicts with the 'mass density 100 kg/m at r/R = 1.0' both sets give. Both sets share the same questionable readings from Figure 2-11 (geometric center 2 m at r/R = 0.0, shear center -3 m and -4 m), which look like y-axis tick labels taken as data, and both give two conflicting values for the same stiffness points (edge 1.4/1.5e11, torsional 0.8/0.9e11, axial 4.5/4.7e10 N). Since A repeats and contradicts itself more without adding any correct fact, B is the cleaner set.
remarks: All numeric claims come from reading plotted curves, so values are inherently approximate; several are clearly wrong rather than merely imprecise (e.g. chordwise positions of 2 m, -3 m, -4 m correspond to axis tick labels, since all colored center curves in Fig. 2-11 lie roughly between -0.3 and 0.9 m). The text layer drops minus signs on the chordwise axis ('4 3 2 1 0 1 2'), which likely caused the misreads. Both sets also state two different values for the same (property, r/R) point in the stiffness and axial plots; at most one of each pair can be right. Quotes are mostly axis/legend labels and do not contain the claimed values, so they do not substantiate the numbers in either set.
